subtitles.text: Imagine a ball moving along a straight road. Its position changes as time passes, and we can draw that motion on a graph.
The horizontal axis represents time. The vertical axis represents the distance the ball has travelled from its starting point.
Choose two points on the curve and connect them with a straight line. The slope of that line gives the average speed over the interval.
Now slide the second point closer to the first. The interval becomes smaller, and the straight line approaches the tangent to the curve.
The slope of this tangent is the instantaneous speed. This is the derivative of position with respect to time.
A steeper tangent means faster motion. A horizontal tangent means the ball is momentarily at rest. A negative slope means it is moving back.
